docs.title: LMS Ads Ecosystem
docs.text:
UX Implementation Plan · LinkedIn Marketing Solutions

Visitors who find LinkedIn Ads pages through search land in isolated dead ends — no links to related specs, tips, or product context. This project designs the navigation and content ecosystem that connects those pages.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Eliminate search-landing dead ends across LinkedIn Ads pages by creating a cohesive IA and navigation ecosystem that increases cross-page navigation between product, tips, and specs pages.

docs.title: Phase Pipeline
docs.text: Phase Focus Tasks 1 — Research Audit current pages · Benchmark competitors Task 1 2 — Architecture FigJam ecosystem map · Select 3 in-scope pages Task 2 3 — Design 4 interlinking concepts · Wireframes (3 pages) Tasks 3–4 4 — Specs Breadcrumb hierarchy · Card rules · Hi-fi designs Tasks 5–6 5 — Production Content brief · AEM handoff · Localization Tasks 7–9

docs.title: Recommended Approach
docs.text:
Design direction

Baseline: Concept D — Breadcrumbs + inline contextual links (lowest AEM lift, SEO benefit)

Enhancement: Concept B — Related content cards at page bottom (low AEM lift, below-fold discovery)

Together these cover hierarchy navigation (breadcrumbs) and cross-page discovery (cards) with minimal new engineering.

docs.title: Brief & Goals
docs.text: Project context, problem statement, and technical foundation

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
LinkedIn Ads content lives across a fragmented set of pages — product overviews, tips & best practices, and technical specs are each separate, siloed destinations. Users who arrive from search hit dead ends: no cross-links, no clear hierarchy, no path to related content.

User pain point: Users entering via search encounter isolated Ads pages with no clear pathways to related content, creating dead ends that disrupt their ability to complete tasks efficiently.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Eliminate search-landing dead ends across LinkedIn Ads pages by creating a cohesive IA and navigation ecosystem that increases cross-page navigation between product, tips, and specs pages.

docs.title: Target Audience
docs.text:
Primary: Digital marketers and advertisers who discover LinkedIn Ads content via organic search and need quick access to ad specs, best practices, and product information to plan and execute campaigns.

Entry behavior: Search-first — users land deep in the content hierarchy (specs or tips pages) and need to discover broader context or adjacent resources.

docs.title: Leaf pages (ad-type specific)
docs.text: Page type Example URL Product overview /advertise/ads/sponsored-content/video-ads Tips & Best Practices /advertise/ads/sponsored-content/video-ads/tips Specs /advertise/ads/sponsored-content/video-ads/specs

docs.title: Hub pages (cross-ad-type)
docs.text:
Hub URL Ads Guide /advertise/ads/ads-guide Objective-Based Advertising /advertise/ads/objective-based-advertising Ads Best Practices /advertise/ads/best-practices Ads main /advertise/ads

LLM optimization context

The Ads Guide hub was recently updated for LLM/AI optimization. Design must support both human navigation and modular, self-contained content units that AI systems can parse. Each spec row and content section should be a discrete, complete unit — not dependent on surrounding context.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Pipeline: Discovery → IA Map → Pattern Exploration → Wireframes → Design Spec → Hi-Fi → Content → Handoff → Localization

AEM component feasibility is validated before every hi-fi commitment.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text:
Layer Tool CMS / Production AEM (Adobe Experience Manager) via LEM Hi-fi design Figma + Our Community Design System IA mapping FigJam Research baseline SEO analytics + competitive benchmarking

Biggest risk: AEM component limitations

Any interlinking or navigation pattern must be validated against what is buildable in AEM before hi-fi commitment. New components require engineering estimates and may impact timeline.

docs.title: KPI
docs.text: Cross-page navigation rate between Ads ecosystem content — measured via analytics on session depth and inter-page click events post-launch.

docs.title: Specs Table
docs.text:
Purpose: Structured 3-column table for ad technical requirements, with named section headers and desktop anchor links.

Property Value Columns Spec · Requirement · Notes Properties sectionTitle (string) · rows (array: spec, requirement, notes) Section headers Image Specs · Copy Specs · Technical Specs Desktop Anchor links above table jump to each section Mobile Table scrolls horizontally · section headers collapse to accordion 
┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│ Spec             │ Requirement     │ Notes            │
├──────────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────────┤
│ File type        │ MP4, MOV        │ H.264 encoding   │
│ Max file size    │ 200 MB          │                  │
│ Aspect ratio     │ 16:9, 1:1, 9:16 │ Varies by format │
└──────────────────┴─────────────────┴──────────────────┘

LLM readability

Each row must be a self-contained unit — spec name + full value + notes in a single row, no sub-rows. This ensures both users scanning and AI systems parsing the page get a complete, discrete data point per row.

AEM assessment required

Required only if AEM does not have a suitable existing table component. Flag for engineering estimate before designing.

docs.title: Task 2 · Ecosystem IA Map
docs.text:
Phase 2 — Architecture

Deliverable ia/lms-ads-ecosystem-ia-map.fig Owner UX Lead Done when Full stakeholder group approves proposed IA and 3 in-scope pages are confirmed

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
• Create FigJam with 3 sections

    Section Purpose Current State Existing page structure, as-is Proposed State Redesigned ecosystem architecture Delta / Changes What's new, what changes, what stays

  • Map the current state — color-code every page as a node; add pain-point sticky to each dead end

    Color Page type 🔵 Blue Hub pages 🟢 Green Product pages 🟠 Orange Tips pages 🟣 Purple Specs pages 🔴 Red Dead ends — add sticky: "Pain point: [what the user can't find here]"

    Label each node: page name · abbreviated URL · breadcrumbs Y/N · primary CTA.

  • Design the proposed state — apply all 6 interlinking patterns

    # Pattern Show in FigJam as 1 Triad linking (must-have) Thick bidirectional arrows between product ↔ tips ↔ specs 2 Hub links Thin arrows from every leaf page → hub page 3 Persistent nav module Box labeled "Ad Type Nav Module" on each node 4 Breadcrumbs Annotate each node: e.g. Advertise > Ads > Video Ads > Specs 5 Related content cards "Related" module box at the bottom of each node 6 Inline contextual links Sticky on product nodes: "Body copy links to Specs + Tips inline"

  • Select 3 in-scope pages — one complete ad-type triad (Product + Tips + Specs)

    Decision criteria: - Highest organic search traffic — confirm with SEO team - All 3 pages exist with substantial content - Document rationale on FigJam node: "In scope because: [reason]"

    Page selection is deferred intentionally

    The IA work surfaces which ad-type triad has the most fragmented ecosystem and highest SEO opportunity — that becomes the design target.

  • IA review checkpoint — stakeholders approve; AEM team flags unbuildable components as red stickies → these become design constraints for Task 4

docs.title: Task 3 · Interlinking Pattern Exploration
docs.text:
Phase 3 — Design

Deliverable wireframes/interlinking-pattern-explorations.fig — 4 lo-fi concept frames Owner UX Lead Done when Pattern direction captured in FigJam with stakeholder sign-off

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Create one annotated lo-fi frame per concept (grayscale, placeholder content).

Concept A — Tab NavConcept B — Related CardsConcept C — Sticky SidebarConcept D — Breadcrumbs + Inline Links

Persistent tabs below global nav 

[ Overview ]  [ Tips & Best Practices ]  [ Specs ]
─────────────
Show on all 3 sibling pages. Active tab underlined; inactive tabs are links.

AEM lift High — new component required Discoverability Best — above fold on every page Tradeoff URL changes on tab click may confuse users who bookmarked a specific page

"You might also need" 2-card module at page bottom

Each page shows 2 cards linking to its sibling pages. Cards use the Ecosystem Card component.

AEM lift Low — likely extends existing card component Discoverability Medium — below fold only Tradeoff Users who don't scroll miss it

Page-family tree always visible; accordion on mobile 

Video Ads
├── Overview
├── Tips & Best Practices  ← active
└── Specs
────────────
Back to Ad Specs Guide

AEM lift Highest — new sidebar component required Discoverability Best — always visible regardless of scroll Tradeoff Highest engineering cost; may conflict with existing LMS templates

Hierarchy breadcrumb trail + contextual links in body copy 

Advertise  >  Ads  >  Video Ads  >  Specs

AEM lift Lowest — breadcrumb component may already exist Discoverability Lower — inline only, author-dependent SEO impact High — breadcrumbs are a structured data / SEO signal

docs.title: Decision Step
docs.text:
• Add a decision comparison table to the Figma file

    Pattern AEM lift Discoverability SEO Mobile A — Tab nav High Above fold Neutral Needs mobile design B — Cards Low Below fold Neutral Works well C — Sidebar Highest Always visible Neutral Complex (accordion) D — Breadcrumbs + inline Lowest Inline only High Works well

    Recommended direction

    Adopt D + B as baseline. Breadcrumbs cover above-content hierarchy; cards cover below-content discovery. Combined AEM lift is low — both patterns are compatible with existing components.

    Flag A and C for future consideration pending AEM component roadmap.

  • Present to stakeholders — capture decision and rationale in FigJam, linked back to the IA map from Task 2

docs.title: Task 6 · Hi-Fi Designs — 3 In-Scope Pages
docs.text:
Phase 4 — Specs

Deliverable designs/lms-ads-ecosystem-hifi.fig Owner UX Lead Done when Design review resolved; version tagged v2 — post-review [date] in Figma history

Design system: Our Community Design System — enable via Figma Assets → Team Libraries.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
• Set up file

    Figma page Contents Page 1 — [Ad Type] Product Desktop + mobile frames Page 2 — [Ad Type] Tips Desktop + mobile frames Page 3 — [Ad Type] Specs Desktop + mobile frames Component Proposals Ecosystem Card + Specs Table specs

    Import existing LMS site shell (header, footer, global nav) — do not recreate from scratch.

  • Product page — desktop 1440px + mobile 375px

    Apply real content from the in-scope ad type. Token map:

    Element Token Page background color/surface/default H1 text/heading-xl Subtitle text/body-lg Primary CTA component/button/primary Breadcrumb — linked color/text/link + text/body-sm Breadcrumb — current color/text/secondary + text/body-sm Body copy text/body-md Inline links color/text/link (underlined on hover) Section dividers color/border/subtle Related card hover shadow/md

    Place inline links per Task 5 placement rules. Use Ecosystem Card for related content module.

  • Tips & Best Practices page — desktop + mobile

    Condition Decision ≤ 5 tips Numbered list — text/heading-sm per title, text/body-md per body 6+ tips System accordion component — reduces scroll length Inline Specs link Style as color/text/link inline in body copy — not a CTA button

  • Specs page — desktop + mobile

    Use Specs Table component. Section structure: Image Specs → Copy Specs → Technical Specs.

    • Desktop: anchor links above table jump to each section
    • Mobile: horizontal table scroll + section headers collapse to accordion
    • Each row must be self-contained (spec + value + notes in one row — no sub-rows)

    LLM readability

    Add Figma annotation: "Each row is self-contained — spec name + full value in one row — for both human scanners and AI systems parsing the page."

  • Document custom components on the Component Proposals page — see Custom Components for specs

  • Design review

    Reviewer Focus Stakeholders Visual design alignment AEM / LEM eng Custom component feasibility SEO team H1s and section headings keyword-aligned

    Resolve every Figma comment. Log changes in version history as v2 — post-review [date].

docs.title: Task 7 · Content Optimizations — 3 Pages
docs.text:
Phase 5 — Production

Deliverable content/content-optimization-brief.md Owner Content + SEO Done when SEO review complete; all feedback incorporated with SEO feedback: inline comments

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
• Audit each of the 3 pages

    For each page, fill in this table:

    Element Current Gap / Issue H1 Meta title Meta description Intro paragraph Internal links present Missing links (per Task 5 rules) Content gaps vs. competitors Redundancy with sibling pages

  • Write recommendations per page

    Format every recommendation as: Current → [text] → Recommended → [text] → Rationale: [1 sentence]

    Cover for each page:

    1. H1 update — if needed for SEO clarity
    2. New inline links — exact placement + link text + destination URL (from Task 5 placement rules)
    3. Related card copy — Card 1 and Card 2: title + 1-line description
    4. Breadcrumb label check — confirm page title matches proposed breadcrumb text; flag any mismatch
    5. Content gap fills — e.g. "Add 1–2 sentence intro to Specs page describing [Ad Type] and linking to product overview"

  • SEO review

    Share brief with SEO team. Request:

    • Keyword alignment for recommended H1s and section headings
    • Meta title and description updates
    • Internal linking equity — do proposed links distribute PageRank appropriately?

    Track all SEO changes with: SEO feedback: [what changed and why] as inline comments in the doc.
